info.title: Meerkat Internal API
info.description:
The API your cluster's services call: Meerkat's public keys, scheduled calls, notifications and the OpenID provider's back end. Port 7070 (7443 over HTTPS). Keep it inside the cluster: never expose it.

Keys, discovery and the probe are open. The scheduler and the notifications each have an access setting in the console (Scheduler > Access, Notifications > Access):

- **None**: no credential.
- **Meerkat token**: `Authorization: Bearer mk_...`, an internal token with the perimeter `schedules` or `notifications`.
- **Cluster token**: the calling pod's ServiceAccount token (Kubernetes only).

An access can also be limited to a list of callers. A credential that is sent is always checked. Changes are recorded in the audit trail. Writes answer 503 with Retry-After while the database is being moved.

tags.description: Public keys and OpenID discovery. Open to every caller.

tags.description: Token and userinfo endpoints for applications that sign users in through Meerkat (Enterprise edition).

tags.description: Calls Meerkat makes to your services on a schedule.

get.description: Verify the identity token Meerkat sends with each request. Retired keys stay listed during their grace period. Cached 5 minutes.
Issuer and key set, at the address the caller used. With the OpenID provider active (Enterprise edition), also its endpoints. Cached 5 minutes, except while the provider is active.

post.description: Sent to the tenant's enabled members, narrowed to the roles and users named, and to those allowed to open its link. The readers are worked out at publication, and the audience named is kept: an account that joins the tenant, or is given a role there, while it is live receives it then, told once for all it missed. With `"tenant": "*"`, each enabled tenant whose notifications are on gets its own copy, with its own id; a tenant where nobody may receive it is skipped, and the answer says which and why. A person in several of these tenants sees one notification naming them, and gets one mail. With `ack`, readers are asked to acknowledge it, and `onAck` names your service, called at each acknowledgement (a `NotificationAckCall`).

200.description: Already published under this key; nobody notified again (sent to every tenant: every copy was)

400.description: Malformed, unknown field, or over 64 KiB

422.description: Refused, with the reason and the field (for example the id missing, notifications off for the tenant, nobody in the audience, or above the cap; sent to every tenant: no tenant received it)

post.summary: An acknowledgement, told to your service
post.description: Called once per acknowledgement, through the route of `onAck`. Sent to every tenant, each copy is called with its own id and tenant.

get.description: Your live notifications, newest first. Filter with `meta.<key>=<value>` or `meta.<key>=~<RE2 regex>`; all must match. One that asks to be acknowledged says where that stands: `ackState`, `acknowledged`, `ackBy`.

delete.description: Withdraws your live notifications that match; at least one meta condition. Filter with `meta.<key>=<value>` or `meta.<key>=~<RE2 regex>`; all must match.

withdrawn.description: The ids of what was withdrawn.

count.description: How many notifications were withdrawn: every copy of one sent to every tenant counts.

400.description: No meta condition, or a malformed one

delete.description: Withdraws the notification your id names: every copy of one sent to every tenant. Its readers see a row saying it was withdrawn, with nothing of what it said, out of their unread count; its mails not sent yet are cancelled. An id none of your notifications carries yet is kept (202) for the life expires gives (30 days by default, 90 at most): the notification arrives withdrawn, and nobody is told.

parameters.name: expires
parameters.description: For a key not received yet: how long it is kept, an ISO 8601 duration or a date. 30 days by default, 90 at most.

200.description: Withdrawn now (`withdrawn`), or already ended before (`already`)

202.description: A key not received yet: kept

400.description: An id with a character it may not carry, or expires that is not a duration or a date, or beyond 90 days

get.description: For one of yours that asks to be acknowledged: who did, when, and who has not yet.

409.description: It does not ask for an acknowledgement

post.summary: Exchange a code or refresh token
post.description: For an application's server inside the cluster. A code or refresh token works only while the user's Meerkat session lasts and a route of the client still admits the user.

401.description: invalid_client: unknown client or wrong secret
Access token missing, invalid or expired

post.description: The token in the Authorization header or as access_token in the form.

access_token.description: When not sent as a bearer.

401.description: Access token missing, invalid or expired

meerkatToken.description: Meerkat token (`mk_...`) with the perimeter `schedules` or `notifications`, or an application administrator's token. Required when the access is Meerkat token; refused when it is Cluster token.

clusterToken.description: The calling pod's ServiceAccount token (/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token). Required when the access is Cluster token. Kubernetes only.

oidcClient.description: Client id and secret (client_secret_basic), or in the form. A public client sends no secret.

oidcAccessToken.description: An access token from the OpenID provider.

CallerRefused.description: Caller not admitted, or token perimeter does not cover this API

ClusterUnavailable.description: Cluster token unavailable: not on Kubernetes, or the Kubernetes API did not answer

Schedule.description: A scheduled call: a route and path, when, and with which roles.

name.description: Shown in the console and the log.

description.description: What it is for, 500 characters at most.

roles.description: Roles the call carries, 10 at most. Rules treat them like a person's.

createdBy.description: Account that last wrote it (a token's owner); empty when only the access mode identified the caller.

caller.description: Who created it, as the access check identified them.

tenantId.description: Tenant the call is made in; also where `$name` vault references resolve. Empty for none.

metadata.description: Your own labels, for `meta.<key>` filters. 20 keys at most; keys of letters, digits and - _ . : up to 40 characters; values up to 200.

method.description: HTTP method. GET and HEAD are refused.

path.description: Path on the route, starting with /.

body.description: An object or array is sent as JSON; a string is sent as is.

contentType.description: Content-Type, when the body is not JSON.

headers.description: Extra headers, 10 at most. Values may be vault references (`$name`). Authorization, Host and the Meerkat-Job headers are refused.

every.description: Cadence: ISO 8601 duration (PT30M, P1D), 1 minute at least, counted from the end of the previous run.

cron.description: Calendar: five-field cron (0 3 * * MON), in timezone.

at.description: Single date, RFC 3339 with offset: runs once.

startAt.description: First run of a cadence or calendar (Unix seconds). Not with at.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for cron (Europe/Paris); empty is UTC.

overlap.description: skip: a run due while the previous one is open waits for it.

catchUp.description: How late a missed run may still go out, in seconds; 0 is no limit.

retryLost.description: Delay before a lost run is sent again, PT1M to P1D. Empty never resends.

timeout.description: Wait for the answer, ISO 8601, 2 minutes at most. Long work answers 202.

nextAt.description: Next run (Unix seconds); 0 once a single date has run.

runId.description: Run in progress (its Meerkat-Job-Run); empty if none.

runStarted.description: Start of the run in progress (Unix seconds).

claimedBy.description: Gateway making the run, when several share the database.

claimedAt.description: When that gateway took or renewed the run (Unix seconds).

runDetail.description: Service's last report on the run.

runState.description: calling: no answer yet; accepted: the service took the work; waiting: lost, to be resent.

attempts.description: Attempts of the current or last run.

runCause.description: manual: run now; replay: past run again; retry: after a failure; asked: the service asked to be called back.

turnTry.description: Attempts the next run already had.

lastAt.description: End of the last run (Unix seconds).

failingSince.description: First failure of the current streak (Unix seconds); absent while runs succeed.

ScheduleInput.description: Give exactly one of every, cron or at. Fields Meerkat manages are ignored.

name.description: Shown in the console and the log.

roles.description: Roles the call carries, 10 at most. Rules treat them like a person's.

role.description: A single role. Not with roles.

tenantId.description: Tenant the call is made in; also where `$name` vault references resolve. Empty for none.

metadata.description: Your own labels, for `meta.<key>` filters. 20 keys at most; keys of letters, digits and - _ . : up to 40 characters; values up to 200.

method.description: HTTP method, POST by default. GET and HEAD are refused.

path.description: Path on the route, / by default.

body.description: An object or array is sent as JSON; a string is sent as is.

contentType.description: Content-Type, when the body is not JSON.

headers.description: Extra headers, 10 at most. Values may be vault references (`$name`). Authorization, Host and the Meerkat-Job headers are refused.

every.description: Cadence: ISO 8601 duration (PT30M, P1D), 1 minute at least, counted from the end of the previous run.

cron.description: Calendar: five-field cron (0 3 * * MON), in timezone.

at.description: Single date, RFC 3339 with offset: runs once.

startAt.description: First run of a cadence or calendar (Unix seconds). Not with at.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for cron (Europe/Paris); empty is UTC.

overlap.description: skip (the only value): a run due while the previous one is open waits for it.

catchUp.description: How late a missed run may still go out, in seconds; 0 is no limit.

retryLost.description: Delay before a lost run (202, then no report) is sent again, PT1M to P1D. Empty never resends.

timeout.description: Wait for the answer, ISO 8601, 2 minutes at most. Long work answers 202.

paused.description: Create paused. Omitted on PUT, keeps the current state.

id.description: History entry id, for a replay.

runId.description: Meerkat-Job-Run sent; absent if never sent.

cause.description: Why it went out, when not a regular run.

state.description: dropped: too late, never sent; lost: the service stopped reporting; cancelled: stopped by someone.

ScheduleRunReport.description: Report on a run accepted with 202.

run.description: Meerkat-Job-Run of the call, or send that header.

state.description: Empty or running: progress (renews the lease). done or failed: closes the run.

detail.description: What to show about the run.

retryIn.description: With failed: call again after this ISO 8601 duration, 1 minute to 1 day. After 5 in a row the run is abandoned.

replayOf.description: History entry to replay, with a new run identifier and the current payload. Empty runs now.

id.description: The id you gave it. The copies of a message sent to every tenant share it, each listed with its tenantId.

sender.description: Who published it, as the access identified them, or their address.

withdrawnAt.description: When it was withdrawn or replaced (endedAs says which); absent while it is live.

ack.description: `single`: the first reader to acknowledge closes it for everyone. `all`: every reader acknowledges, complete when the last one did. Absent when it asks for none.

onAck.description: Where your service is called at each acknowledgement.

ackCompleteAt.description: Unix seconds the request was closed: the first acknowledgement (single), the last reader's (all).

ackState.description: With `ack`: whether it is still waiting.

ackBy.description: With `ack` single, once done: who closed it.

endedAs.description: How it ended before its time, withdrawnAt being when.

replacedBy.description: Replaced: the notification that replaced it.

exercise.description: Sent to practise: it keeps its realistic level and its audience, and carries the label EXERCISE on the page, the snackbar, the desktop notification and the mail.

mails.description: For one sent with mail: its readers' mails counted by state. pending (to send), sending (a node is sending it), accepted (by the relay: the most the gateway knows, never delivered), failed (the relay refused it for good, 5yz, or a temporary refusal, 4yz, lasted past 24 hours), unknown (the connection went after the end of the data, or the node sending it stopped: never sent again on its own), cancelled (the notification was withdrawn, replaced or expired first), noaddress (the reader has no address).

audienceRoles.description: The roles named at publication, kept: someone given one of them later, while it is live, receives it then.

audienceUsers.description: The accounts named at publication, kept.

NotificationAction.description: A button the reader's browser calls through the data plane, with their session.

route.description: Route serving it; absent for an external link.

method.description: How it is called. GET for one sent without a method.

body.description: The JSON value sent with it; absent when it sends none.

LocalizedText.description: The text, under the key "". A notification sent earlier with one text per language: the reader gets theirs, then English.

crv.description: P-256 for EC, Ed25519 for OKP.

keys.description: Active key of each algorithm, then retired keys in their grace period.

OpenIdConfiguration.description: Without the OpenID provider (Enterprise edition): issuer, keys and algorithms only.

userinfo_endpoint.description: Enterprise edition, with a client declared: on this plane.

error.description: invalid_request, invalid_client, invalid_grant, unsupported_grant_type, invalid_token, server_error, temporarily_unavailable.

code_verifier.description: authorization_code: PKCE verifier, required without a secret.

refresh_token.description: refresh_token: the last one issued; each use returns a new one.

client_id.description: When not in the Authorization header.

client_secret.description: client_secret_post: confidential clients only, not with the Authorization header.

id_token.description: JWT, RS256, audience the client id.

refresh_token.description: Valid while the user's Meerkat session lasts.

OidcUserinfo.description: sub and the claims the route adds; registered claims (iss, aud, exp...) left out.

NotificationTarget.description: `{service, path}` for a service behind Meerkat, or `{url}` outside it. Name the service as called in the cluster (station-ui for station-ui.prod.svc.cluster.local) and the path as it sees it; Meerkat builds the public address from its route. An external url must be https.

service.description: Service host name in the cluster.

path.description: Path as the service sees it.

method.description: Any case; stored in upper case.

body.description: Any JSON value, sent as is with `Content-Type: application/json`. Not with GET. Counts in the message's 64 KiB. The reader can see it: put nothing secret in it.

NotificationActionInput.description: A button: a label, a link, and how the reader's browser calls it. On an external url, a method other than GET with a body makes the browser ask the site first (CORS preflight): the site must allow it.

NotificationMessage.description: 64 KiB at most. Unknown fields are refused.

id.description: Required, a UUID of your choice: it lets you retry without duplicates, replace or withdraw the notification, and follow its acknowledgements and mails. Meerkat never makes one up. Scoped by its source, the caller the internal plane recognises (a token's name, a ServiceAccount, the workload behind the address): published again from the same source under an id already used, before it expires, even after it was withdrawn or replaced, it returns that notification, creates nothing and tells nobody; the content is not compared. Your actions are called with notification=<id>, and onAck receives it.

tenant.description: Tenant id or name; optional with a single one. Must be enabled, with notifications on. `*` sends a copy to every tenant: named users each tenant has, the others ignored there.

roles.description: Only members holding one of these roles. Kept with the notification: an account that joins the tenant, or is given a role there, while it is live receives it then (one news and one digest mail for all it missed).

users.description: Only these members, by username. With roles, either matches. Kept with the notification: an account that joins the tenant, or is given a role there, while it is live receives it then (one news and one digest mail for all it missed).

title.description: Required. Plain text, 200 characters at most.

detail.description: Where it leads: a service and path, or an https url.

mail.description: Also send by mail; needs a mail relay. The mails are queued in the database, one per reader with an address, sent one at a time by the nodes: a node that stops leaves the rest to the next. A temporary refusal is tried again for 24 hours, a permanent one fails; the outcomes are counted in mails.

expires.description: ISO 8601 duration (P7D) or RFC 3339 date; default 30 days, 90 at most.

ack.description: Ask the readers to acknowledge it: `single`, the first one closes it for everyone (on call); `all`, every reader must (a safety instruction). While a reader owes it, they cannot delete it.

onAck.description: Your service, `{service, path}` only: Meerkat POSTs a `NotificationAckCall` to it through its route at each acknowledgement, as the user `meerkat` in the notification's tenant with no role, retried twice. Needs `ack`.

replaces.description: The id of an earlier notification of yours: it ends as replaced when this one is published, and leaves its readers' list and count, the replacement standing in its place; its mails not sent yet are cancelled. Sent to every tenant, every copy. An id not received yet is kept as long as this notification lives: arriving later, it is stored already replaced. The replacement has an id of its own.

exercise.description: Sent to practise: it keeps its realistic level and its audience, and carries the label EXERCISE on the page, the snackbar, the desktop notification and the mail.

id.description: The id you gave. Sent to every tenant, the id of the whole send.

recipients.description: Number of recipients; sent to every tenant, the sum of the copies.

existing.description: The id was already used, before it expired: the earlier notification, nobody notified again. Sent to every tenant: true when every copy was.

tenants.description: Sent to every tenant: the tenants that received a copy, under the one id.

existing.description: Key already used in this tenant.

skipped.description: Sent to every tenant: the tenants left out, and why.

state.description: The notification answered is not live: its id was withdrawn or replaced before, or named by a withdrawal or a replacement before it arrived. Nobody was told.

replaced.description: With replaces: the id it ended now.

NotificationPublished.description: The id is the one you gave: replace, withdraw and follow the notification with it. Sent to every tenant, it names the whole send; tenants lists the tenants that received a copy, skipped those left out.

NotificationPerson.description: A person, as an acknowledgement names them.

username.description: Empty if the account no longer exists.

name.description: Full name, when the account has one.

missing.description: Who has not yet; empty once a single one is closed.

NotificationAcks.description: Where an acknowledgement stands, person by person.

NotificationAckCall.description: What your `onAck` service receives at each acknowledgement, as a POST with a JSON body. Headers: `Meerkat-Notification` (its id) and `Meerkat-Attempt`. Answer 2xx; anything else is tried twice more.

acknowledged.description: Readers who acknowledged it so far.

complete.description: This acknowledgement closed it: the first (single), the last (all).

withdrawn.description: The id, when this call withdrew it.

already.description: The id, when it had ended before: a call sent again changes nothing.

pending.description: The id, which none of your notifications carries yet: kept, and the notification will be stored withdrawn when it arrives.

post.description: Sent through the schedule's route, with its method (POST by default), body and headers. The same run may arrive twice: ignore a Meerkat-Job-Run already seen.

parameters.name: Meerkat-Job-Run
parameters.description: Run identifier, the same on every attempt of a run.

202.description: Accepted: report progress and the outcome with PATCH /api/schedules/{id}/run

424.description: Not now: call again after Retry-After. 5 times in a row at most

Retry-After.description: Seconds or an HTTP date, kept between 1 minute and 1 day.

default.description: Failed. No answer, 401, 403, 404, 502, 503 and 504 are tried again, 3 attempts at most
